name: Sankarism
summary: Sankarism is the programme of Thomas Sankara's 1983-87 revolution in Burkina Faso: a self-described democratic and popular, anti-imperialist revolution that smashed the neocolonial state, mobilised the people through Committees for the Defence of the Revolution, and sought a planned, self-sufficient economy free of foreign debt and aid. It put women's emancipation, health, literacy and reforestation at the centre, and combined pan-African non-alignment with austere, anti-corruption leadership. In power it also dissolved old parties, set up revolutionary tribunals and crushed a teachers' strike.
scope: The doctrine and record of Sankara's National Council of the Revolution (1983-1987): the Political Orientation Speech, his speeches on women, debt, ecology and the UN, and the regime's documented acts. Later parties that use the label (which split over Marxism) and recent leaders compared to Sankara are excluded.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Orientation Speech builds a revolutionary army with defence of territorial integrity as its external duty, and Burkina kept its army.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Orientation Speech names forces drawing power from the traditional structures of feudal society as enemies of the people and calls for abolishing the traditional structures that oppress peasants.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The regime nationalised land and mineral wealth by law.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The Orientation Speech pledges solidarity with movements fighting for national liberation, naming SWAPO, the Sahrawis and the Palestinians.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sankara asked at the OAU for a limit on the arms race among poor countries and at the UN made disarmament a permanent goal.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The CNR dissolved the parties tied to the old regime on taking power and Sankara said reactionaries sheltering in underground parties would be blocked.

central-planning.rationale: The Orientation Speech's goal is 'an independent national economy, self-sufficient and planned' with effective control of production and distribution circuits, and a five-year plan was drawn up.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The Orientation Speech calls for drawing only on what is good in traditions and rejects the decadent values of feudal traditional culture, and the 1987 speech denounces dowries and forced widow-marriage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sankara held that development models imposed from outside must be rejected and attacked colonial and neocolonial rule as plunder.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Orientation Speech says exploiting classes understand only 'the revolutionary class struggle' and describes workers' wage struggles against neocolonial employers as endless, rejecting partnership between classes.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Sankara called the revolution the result of a historical process in which social classes struggle against each other, and the Orientation Speech frames Voltaic history as struggle between exploiting classes and the people.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Sankara said the West owes Africa a debt of blood that the greatest riches could not repay, and traced the debt to colonialism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Orientation Speech and UN speech condemn colonial exploitation of the country for the benefit of the colonizer.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The 1987 speech condemns women's crass materialism and greed for jewellery as destructive of revolutionary commitment, and the Orientation Speech criticises the capitalist consumer society.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Orientation Speech treats chiefs and feudal-traditional forces as allies of the reactionary bourgeoisie that must be curbed, giving them no official role.

death-penalty.rationale: Scholarship records executions of several unionists and officers for alleged coup plotting under Sankara, and he threatened that looting CDR members would be shot.

decide-locally.rationale: The Orientation Speech calls for decentralisation and devolution of administrative power to bring government closer to the people, within democratic centralism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Scholars describe Sankara as urging delinking from Western dependency, but he also committed to trade with all countries on equal terms and kept Western ties.

direct-action.rationale: The August Revolution was a mass insurrection and the Orientation Speech has the CDRs act as assault detachments mobilising people for revolutionary action rather than parliamentary routes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Orientation Speech wants women equal to men in all domains and involved at every level of national decisions.

dominated-front.rationale: Sankara proposed a united front of African states against the debt and described the non-aligned world as a solidarity of the dominated.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Orientation Speech puts the interest of the masses before self-interest, and at the UN he spoke of rights drawing strength from awareness of duties.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Orientation Speech commits to trade with all countries on an equal footing for mutual benefit, so it rejects a bloc shut off from outside trade.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime replaced ordinary courts with People's Revolutionary Tribunals that punished counter-revolutionaries and corruption without ordinary legal protections.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: At the UN Sankara said the United Nations must be strengthened and given the means to act, endorsing the Secretary-General's proposals.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As a non-aligned state Burkina stayed outside the great-power blocs, and Sankara called for disarmament and freedom from big-power hindrance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Sankara declared men and women equal with equal rights and responsibilities, nationalities equal, and called apartheid Nazism because people are humans, not animals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Orientation Speech treats Burkina as a nation of many nationalities living in equality, with ethnic prejudice to be fought.

experts-over-public.rationale: At the UN Sankara swore that nothing would be done in Burkina without the people's own participation and decision, and in 1986 said a handful of engineers and experts would never save the forests without a popular struggle.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Orientation Speech promises remunerative prices and industrial units to give farmers markets for their produce in every season.

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: The Orientation Speech says emancipation is not drinking, smoking and wearing trousers like men, and the 1987 speech rejects a feminism that demands the right to be masculine.

free-trade.rationale: The Orientation Speech complains of unfair competition from imports and sets 'trade on an equal footing and mutual benefit' as the principle, not free trade.

future-generations.rationale: Scholarship quotes Sankara on reforestation as a duty for the living and for those yet to be born.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The 1987 speech calls the earlier Ministry of Women a pseudoministry and says 'we don't need another apparatus led by women' to control women's lives, preferring a plan across all ministries.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The 1987 speech holds that women's inequality was produced by social transition and class structure, not by physical attributes.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Orientation Speech condemns the parasitic bourgeoisie for living on fabulous rents and ill-gotten gains from others' work.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Orientation Speech says neocolonialism changed only the form of imperialist exploitation and that independence requires transforming the society's socio-economic foundations.

independent-unions.rationale: Sankara said he would block reactionaries in unions and wanted no rivalry between unions and CDRs, and after the 1985 teachers' strike the regime dismissed about 1,300 teachers and arrested leaders.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Sankara repeatedly claimed rights of peoples, including independence, free choice of government and a new economic order.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: At the UN Sankara claimed the right to the free choice of the form and structure of government and to organisation adapted to Burkinabe civilization, rejecting outside diktats.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: At the UN Sankara called Palestinians and Jews anti-Zionist and condemned Israel's policy, yet said Israel's people should learn to be a nation like others.

land-redistribution.rationale: Scholarship records land distribution to the landless among the regime's first measures, and the Orientation Speech calls for land reform abolishing barriers that oppress peasants.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was nationalised with the farmers' right to till it guaranteed, so individuals hold land by use.

leader-cult.rationale: Scholarship describes Sankara as resisting personality cults and idolatry, and he refused to place his portrait in offices.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The regime's tribunals punished lazy workers, and the Orientation Speech says all Voltaics of working age will be required for the national work site.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The 1987 speech calls prostitution a mark of female slavery and says the revolution works to eliminate practices that demean women, including prostitution.

local-production.rationale: Sankara urged 'produce in Africa, process in Africa and consume in Africa', consuming what is produced instead of importing, and the Orientation Speech sets food self-sufficiency as the first struggle.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The stated aim is a planned national economy with popular control over the circuits of production and distribution, and the speech attacks speculators and traders who sabotage supply.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The 1987 women's speech credits dialectical materialism and says social position is determined by the economic structure and level of technological development, not biology.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Orientation Speech rejects an apolitical army and gives it the task of maintaining revolutionary order and safeguarding popular power internally.

minority-language-support.rationale: Sankara backed a radio service reaching the country in the languages compatriots understand.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Orientation Speech asks militants to put the masses' interest above self-interest and expect no reward, and the regime relied on volunteer labour on railways and housing.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Orientation Speech wants the people to be 'sole master of the material and immaterial wealth of the nation' and protects against the looting of resources, and the regime nationalised land and minerals.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Orientation Speech pledges respect for independence and sovereignty and backs the national rights of Namibia, Western Sahara and Palestine.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Orientation Speech calls for a planned national economy, land reform, school reform and state control of production and distribution circuits, far beyond defence, justice and property protection.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Orientation Speech condemns the state bourgeoisie's favouritism, nepotism and influence-peddling in the use of public office for business.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sankara denounced the foreign listening and detection centres on African soil as serving exploiters, not Africans.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The 1987 speech says rich and educated women should place their wealth and knowledge at the service of the people.

one-party-rule.rationale: Asked about a single party after 1983, Sankara said it could be too restrictive and the regime governed through the CNR and CDRs without a single ruling party.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: The 1987 speech condemns polygamy and the regime banned forced marriage and polygamy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Orientation Speech made the CDRs organs through which people take part in decisions, and scholarship records that they gave previously excluded poor citizens a role, though some CDRs acted in a commandist way and policy was set from above.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The 1987 speech states that inequality was institutionalised in the transition between societies, that social cohesion defined by men requires women's subjugation, and that the home reproduces male domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Orientation Speech sets school reform to build a Voltaic personality and a culture magnifying dignity, courage and nationalism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Sankara joined patriotic and class language throughout ('Homeland or death'), and the Orientation Speech calls for a nationalist culture magnified alongside a revolution of workers and peasants.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Orientation Speech says the people cannot entrust defence to a group of men and will assume its own defence, the army being only a more specialised posting, though a regular revolutionary army remained.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The Orientation Speech has the army farm and build, and calls on everyone able to work to join the national work site.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Orientation Speech attacks the state bourgeoisie for large-scale corruption, misappropriation, influence-peddling and nepotism while holding office.

premarital-sex.rationale: The 1987 speech rejects ostracising unmarried women and young mothers and says single women can flourish, placing blame on men.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Orientation Speech wants a national, revolutionary and popular culture that celebrates national dignity and draws on what is good in traditions.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Orientation Speech makes the revolution that of the immense majority for the immense majority, with the poorest peasants first among the beneficiaries.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Orientation Speech has the people and a revolutionary army take over defence, and the regime set up popular tribunals in place of ordinary courts, leaving no place for private provision.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Orientation Speech says the state bourgeoisie used the state as industrial capitalists use their means of production to accumulate gains from exploiting workers' labour power, and speaks of the shameless exploitation behind landlords' rents.

property-fundamental.rationale: The regime nationalised land and mineral wealth by law, guaranteeing farmers' right to till the land.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Sankara called apartheid a cancer and modern Nazism, and Burkina boycotted it politically, culturally and economically.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The new government rejected the IMF's loan conditionality, and Sankara opposed assistance from the IMF and World Bank as reinforcing neocolonialism.

rent-control.rationale: The Orientation Speech sets a policy to stop speculation and excessive rents, with 'reasonable rents' and large-scale housing construction.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: Sankara's slogan was 'Homeland or death', and at the UN he said the slave who will not rebel does not deserve pity.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: After the 1985 general strike the regime dismissed about 1,300 civil servants and jailed strikers, restricting strike action in practice.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: At the UN Sankara called for a new international economic order, doing away with the old order and winning decision-making rights over world trade and monetary machinery.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Orientation Speech asks militants to lead by moral example, yet the regime also relied on tribunals, sanctions and force, so the record points both ways.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Orientation Speech demands a revolutionary morality free of corruption, theft, lies and individualism, with the masses' interest placed ahead of self-interest.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: At the UN Sankara said aid had left his country disorganised and encouraged only aid that helps manage without it, and the regime refused IMF conditionality, though budget support from abroad persisted.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1987 speech attacks men's total control over women at home, urges women to live free of the male protectorate, and says men and women will share all tasks in the home.

simple-living.rationale: At the UN Sankara said Burkina was learning to live simply and demanding austerity of itself, and urged Africans to live African.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Orientation Speech states that the revolution 'will proceed with the destruction of the neocolonial state machine' and build a new one, converting the laws, administration, courts, police and army.

socialized-care.rationale: The 1987 speech calls for a large-scale network of nurseries, day-care centres and cafeterias so women can join revolutionary action, with men sharing housework.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In 1987 Sankara told the OAU that the debt cannot be repaid and proposed a united front refusing payment.

space-expansion.rationale: In 1986 Sankara urged that 1 percent of the money spent seeking life on other planets finance saving trees on Earth.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Orientation Speech describes the colonial and neocolonial administration, army, courts and school as instruments shaped to serve imperialism and the reactionary classes, and the state bourgeoisie as using the state apparatus to accumulate wealth.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Orientation Speech has the state play a fundamental economic role, with a plan and control of production and distribution, and the regime directed railway, dam and housing building.

state-harmful.rationale: Sankara's aim was a new 'people's democratic state', replacing the neocolonial machine rather than abolishing the state.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sankara placed Burkina among the non-aligned countries and said his country's camp was Burkina Faso.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The CNR dissolved the old regime's parties, said reactionaries in unions or underground parties must be blocked, and the regime jailed striking teachers and was heavy-handed with opposition currents.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Orientation Speech wants agriculture protected from unfair competition by imports, and Sankara urged consuming what Burkina produces rather than importing.

taxation-theft.rationale: The regime enhanced tax collection and abolished the colonial-era head tax, treating taxation as a legitimate state tool.

total-state.rationale: The Orientation Speech assigns the National Council of the Revolution the design, management and control of national life, political, economic and social, and calls for revolutionising every sector including culture and school.

trade-surplus.rationale: The Orientation Speech says an economy that buys more abroad than it sells is gradually ruined, citing the 25 percent export cover of imports.

traditional-family.rationale: The 1987 speech attacks the patriarchal family as an institution of women's domestic slavery and says marriage is not indispensable.

unions-good.rationale: Sankara counted on progressive unions and denounced reactionary ones, while his regime crushed the 1985 teachers' strike, so the record points both ways.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Orientation Speech sets 'a health to everyone' as the objective, with maternal and child care and immunisation, and the regime built a clinic per village and ran mass vaccination.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: The 1987 speech says the housewife works without pay and that society turns women into objects of exploitation for their labour power.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sankara said women's status will improve only by eliminating the exploitative system and that liberation requires an upheaval in the means of production and all social relations.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: The regime founded the Women's Union of Burkina as women's own framework and Sankara said women must put forward their own demands, while denying a sex war against men.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Orientation Speech has women take part at all levels of decision and execution, and the 1987 speech condemns earlier regimes for ignoring women's civil and political rights.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The Orientation Speech says power must pass to 'the alliance of classes constituting the people', naming the working class as a revolutionary class and the peasantry as the main force by numbers.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The Orientation Speech allows that some middle-bourgeois elements may be sympathetic and objectively on the people's side, but demands 'revolutionary mistrust' toward them, so the alliance is conditional.

workers-nation.rationale: In 1986 Sankara described the fight against apartheid as proceeding by 'proletarian internationalism' in unity with other peoples' action.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Orientation Speech and later interviews hold that imperialism drains the country's wealth through foreign investment, debt and trade and is the main cause of backwardness.

notes: Positions rest on Sankara's speeches and the regime's documented record (parties dissolved, tribunals, 1985 teachers' strike, land nationalisation); where a record exists it answers instead of the speeches. Themes searched with no recorded position: religion and church-state relations, criminal justice beyond tribunals, immigration, sexuality, drugs, technology policy, taxation of wealth, media regulation, electoral design, central banking. The Pathfinder anthology and journal articles were unavailable, so the record rests on the speeches available online plus two dissertations and one review. Contemporary Sankarist parties differ on Marxism, so no single party platform is used.

keyFigures.role: Leader of the 1983 revolution and president of Burkina Faso until his killing in 1987
